bull_bear.body: Debt repayment (deleveraging); Funding organic expansion (new colleges, geographies); Demerger to allow separate capital raising for Commerce vertical; Potential future M&A for global university assets via SNVA.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Lower CA pass percentages impacting demand; Regulatory delays in demerger (NCLT/SEBI); Execution risk in scaling 15 new colleges simultaneously; Faculty attraction/retention in Tier 2/3 towns; Impairment risks in non-core assets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, focused on 'unlocking value' via demerger and structural profitability; Emphasizes disciplined execution and long-term vision (FY30 goals); Transparent about near-term margin trade-offs for growth.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The demerger splits assets roughly 65% (Commerce) to J.K. Shah entity and 35% to remaining Veranda; Warrants issued for prior acquisitions will be proportionately split between the two entities; Management views the 'Junior IAS' and integrated K-12-to-Professional pipeline as a unique moat against pure-play test prep competitors.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Maiden QIP" in Jul 2025 raising "~₹357 Cr", deployed for "QIP-led deleveraging", alongside "Debt refinancing — Optimized debt structure and cost".
- Demerger rationale is capital-allocation led: "Post demerger, both businesses will have sharper strategic focus, greater operational agility and dedicated capital allocation"; separate listing enables "focused capital allocation & value creation".
- Portfolio pruning: "Sep 2025: Divesting Vocational segment to SNVA Veranda. Ltd." — "The divestment of Vocational Segment (Edureka, Veranda Higher Ed & Six Phrase) to SNVA EduTech Ltd."
- Shareholder consideration in the demerger is "1:1 share allotment. Every Veranda shareholder receives one share in the newly listed JK Shah Commerce entity at no additional cost". No dividend policy is stated.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- J.K. Shah Classes has over four decades of producing All India Rankers across CA, CS and CMA, giving the Commerce vertical institutional brand depth few commerce platforms can match
- ACCA exemptions of up to nine papers for qualified CAs give Indian finance professionals a differentiated, direct route into a globally recognised qualification
- Integrated B.Com-plus-professional-certification pathway lets students pursue a formal degree while simultaneously preparing for CA/CS/CMA, described as a genuine market differentiator
- Pan-India Preferred Delivery Centre network with vernacular-language coaching extends reach into Tier 2/3 cities underserved by English-only competitors
- Partnership with Cambridge University Press & Assessment gives Veranda K-12 schools access to globally recognised curricula and credentialing
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Student Acquisition Risk — Changes in student enrolment patterns, competitive intensity, and shifting demand for professional and test-preparation courses may impact revenue growth across Academic Delivery, Commerce, CA/ACCA and Test Preparation businesses.
- Faculty and Talent Risk — Dependence on experienced faculty, trainers and leadership personnel for academic excellence and student outcomes across all education verticals; key-person dependency could affect delivery quality and continuity.
- Technology and Digital Platform Risk — System failures, platform downtime, or inability to keep pace with evolving digital learning technologies could impact learner experience across online and hybrid delivery models.
- Regulatory and Compliance Risk — Changes in education regulations, data privacy laws, taxation and corporate governance requirements may impact operations across all business segments.
- Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Risk — Unauthorised access, data breaches, ransomware attacks or compromise of student and employee information affecting digital learning platforms and corporate functions.
- Integration and Acquisition Risk — Challenges in integrating acquired businesses, systems, processes and cultures across group-wide operations may affect expected synergies, relevant given the Company's history of multiple acquisitions.
- Economic and Market Risk — Macroeconomic uncertainty, inflationary pressures, changes in consumer spending and employment trends may affect demand for educational services across all business segments.
- Competition Risk — Increasing competition from edtech companies, coaching institutes, universities and global online learning providers across all business verticals.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Commerce: Strong performance, core driver of profitability; Non-Commerce (Govt Prep + Academic): Outperformed expectations, Govt Prep saw INR 5cr impairment but otherwise positive EBITDA; Vocational: Partial divestment to SNVA Veranda, retaining one North American entity temporarily.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as "One of the Leading Education Players in India" with a "Technology driven, asset light & scalable business model" and tagline "Affordability | High-quality Content | Outcome-oriented Approach".
- Growth strategy is explicitly acquisition-led: "Successfully acquired legacy brands which are market leaders in their respective segments" (Veranda Race, Edureka, J. K. Shah Classes, Chennai Race BTA, 6 companies in May 2023, Tapasya, BB Publications & Navkar).
- In Commerce it claims "Market Leader #1 in CA, CS, CMA, ACCA"; in Government Test Prep it claims a "Leading presence in South India" via RACE with a "Diverse exam portfolio: UPSC | SSC | Banking | TNPSC | KPSC | State PSC and others".
- Current phase is branded "Veranda 2.0" — "Built strong. Scaling smarter with Veranda 2.0" — versus "Veranda 1.0" (Dec 2020 start) and the "New Launches, IPO Listing and M&A" phase (listed on BSE & NSE in Apr 2022 at INR 137).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] Composite scheme of demerger of the Commerce vertical: Board approval Sep 2025, filed with NSE/BSE Sep 2025, exchange NOC Jan 2026, filed with NCLT Jan 2026, NCLT-directed CCM Mar 2026, CCM held and approved Apr 2026 (meeting held April 24, 2026), second motion filed Apr 2026, NCLT hearing "Orders Reserved on July 20, 2026", with "Listing in September 2026" of JK Shah Commerce Education Limited.
- [Demerger outlook] "Targeting 3-4x revenue growth via product and geographical expansion over 3-4 years; INR 1,000+ Cr revenue expected by FY30"; Commerce FY30 aspirations are "₹1,000+ Cr Revenue, 8 lakh+ Enrolments, 50%+ EBITDA Margin".
- [Divestment / JV] SNVA Veranda Ltd brings together "Veranda's domestic strength" and "SNVA's international network": "60+ Countries" presence, "1.5 million+ Trained Learners", combined presence across India, USA, UK, France, Italy, Malta, Switzerland and Singapore; FY27 targets of "₹250+ Cr Revenue", "₹50+ crore EBITDA", "2 lakh+ / year Learner Base" and "60+ countries", with FY26-FY30 outlook of 25% revenue CAGR, 35% EBITDA CAGR and "3x over 4 years" learner base.
- [Partnerships] "Feb 2025: Signed MoU with IIT Madras", "Jun 2025: Launches CIAP with IAB", "Jul 2023: Partnership with Logic School of mgmt."
- [Leadership] Chairman & Executive Director Mr. Kalpathi S Suresh — B.Tech. from IIT Madras, M.S. from Clemson University, selected for the 'Outstanding Entrepreneur of the Year' in 1999 by Ernst & Young, India.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Veranda Learning Solutions Ltd. delivers commerce professional-qualification coaching (CA, CS, CMA, CFA, CPA, ACCA), K-12 managed-school academic services, and government/competitive-exam test preparation (UPSC, banking, SSC, TNPSC, state PSCs) to school-age learners through working professionals across India. Programmes are delivered in offline, online, hybrid and blended formats through a pan-India network of Preferred Delivery Centres (PDCs) reaching Tier 2/3 cities, with a 50% economic interest retained in SNVA Veranda Limited (formerly SNVA EduTech) for vocational training and global higher-education pathways in the US and Europe.

outlook.body: FY27 Revenue: ~INR 670cr (+40% YoY); FY27 PAT: >INR 144cr; Margin: Slight dip in Commerce EBITDA % due to new college OpEx/capex, recovering in FY28; Order Inflow: Targeting 19k+ students in managed colleges (+15%); Capex/Commissioning: 15 new managed commerce colleges in FY27; Karnataka expansion for Govt Prep.

outlook.body: Enrollments reached 2.5 lakh students (+21% YoY); Collections at INR 449cr (+40% YoY); Managed college student base expected to grow from 17k to 19k+ in FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Demerger of J.K. Shah Commerce (targeting INR 1,000cr revenue by FY30); Expansion of managed colleges into Tier 2/3 districts (15 new centers); Geographic expansion of Govt Prep into Karnataka, Andhra, Telangana; SNVA Veranda global university network expansion (US, Europe, Singapore).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Demerger of the Commerce vertical into J.K. Shah Commerce Education Ltd. to create an independent, focused entity with its own capital access, dedicated management, governance and market visibility, paving the way for a separate listing
- Restructured the Vocational and Global Higher Education segment into a 50:50 partnership with SNVA Veranda Limited to access an international ecosystem (university ownership, study-abroad pathways) while retaining a 50% economic interest without the balance-sheet intensity of direct international expansion
- Built leadership depth and demerger readiness at the Commerce vertical through structured mentoring, clearer accountability frameworks and targeted external hiring ahead of the planned independent listing
- Going-forward financial priorities: sustainable growth, prudent capital allocation, stronger cash generation and improving return metrics across businesses
- Tightening fundamentals internally: optimising working capital cycles, improving collections, rationalising costs and strengthening operating efficiency, with selective investment prioritising scalability, learner engagement and long-term returns
- Academics segment moving toward an asset-light managed-services model to participate across the K-12 value chain while improving capital efficiency, including expansion of managed school services, AI-enabled learning initiatives and digital-marketing-led admissions
- Government Test Preparation: strengthen market presence through established brands, academic expertise and regional reach, with opportunities to expand digital offerings and increase penetration in under-served geographies
- Realise integration synergies from prior acquisitions through integrated academic operations, common technology platforms, centralised support functions and optimised student-acquisition strategies
- Evaluate industry consolidation and strategic partnerships with educational institutions, universities, corporates and technology providers to widen growth prospects and market reach
- Internal group simplification: proposed amalgamation of Veranda IAS Learning Solutions Private Limited and Neyyar Academy Private Limited into Veranda Race Learning Solutions Private Limited, subject to regulatory approvals, to streamline the Group structure and enhance operational efficiencies
- Management describes a focus on deleveraging and improving cash generation to strengthen the capital structure, including debt optimisation via premature redemption of Non-Convertible Debentures during the year. The Company raised equity capital through a Qualified Institutional Placement to fund its growth plans. Going forward, management states it remains focused on margin expansion, prudent capital allocation and cash flow improvement; the proposed demerger of the Commerce vertical into a separate entity is also framed as a step toward more optimised, entity-specific capital allocation.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Veranda's FY27 expansion plans center on four priorities: geographic expansion, portfolio diversification, deepening presence across the education value chain, and strengthening existing verticals. The Government Test Preparation business plans to expand into Karnataka (using localised content, faculty capabilities and offline coaching infrastructure for KPSC and other state-level exams) and to build a stronger offline presence across North and West India, particularly Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Gujarat, to reduce regional concentration risk. In Commerce Education, around 15 new offline college locations are planned to accelerate growth and improve brand visibility and enrolments. The Company also plans to enter the Pre-KG managed-school segment and further expand its managed K-12 school portfolio as part of a long-term strategy to deepen engagement across the education lifecycle. Separately, the vocational/global higher-education business was restructured into a 50%-owned partnership (SNVA Veranda Limited, formerly SNVA EduTech Limited), which is projected to impact more than 200,000 learners annually, with a potential public listing envisaged at an appropriate stage. During the year the Group also completed a Qualified Institutional Placement and undertook debt optimisation (premature redemption of NCDs) to strengthen its balance sheet ahead of this expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained demand for government employment examinations across central/state government, PSUs and banking institutions, with increasing participation in competitive exams, is expected to support growth in Government Test Preparation
- India's higher education sector continues to expand, supported by rising enrolment levels, National Education Policy (NEP) reforms and growing emphasis on employability, creating opportunities in higher-education services and university partnerships
- The Indian education sector remains fragmented across segments, creating opportunities for consolidation and selective inorganic expansion
- Education remains a priority household expenditure, but prolonged macroeconomic uncertainty (slowdown, inflation, lower disposable income or employment prospects) could impact demand in certain discretionary learning segments and delay enrolment decisions
- Increasing availability of free educational content, self-learning platforms, AI-enabled learning tools and low-cost digital courses is shaping learner preferences and pricing dynamics across the sector, requiring continued investment in content quality and technology
- A significant share of the test-preparation business is linked to government recruitment and professional-qualification examination cycles, so delays in exam schedules or recruitment notifications can affect enrolment cycles and revenue visibility
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Veranda turned structurally profitable in FY26 (PAT INR 130cr vs INR 252cr loss) driven by operating leverage and cost discipline, with the imminent demerger of its high-margin commerce vertical (J.K. Shah) set to unlock sum-of-the-parts value. Guidance for FY27 targets 40% revenue growth to INR 670cr, fueled by aggressive expansion of managed colleges and government test prep, despite near-term margin pressure from new center setup costs.

Dependence on experienced faculty, trainers and leadership personnel for academic excellence and student outcomes across all education verticals; key-person dependency could affect delivery quality and continuity.
System failures, platform downtime, or inability to keep pace with evolving digital learning technologies could impact learner experience across online and hybrid delivery models.
Changes in education regulations, data privacy laws, taxation and corporate governance requirements may impact operations across all business segments.
Unauthorised access, data breaches, ransomware attacks or compromise of student and employee information affecting digital learning platforms and corporate functions.

Challenges in integrating acquired businesses, systems, processes and cultures across group-wide operations may affect expected synergies, relevant given the Company's history of multiple acquisitions.

Increasing competition from edtech companies, coaching institutes, universities and global online learning providers across all business verticals.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Veranda Learning Solutions is a listed Indian education company operating across Commerce test-prep, Academics (K-12 managed schools) and Government competition test-preparation, alongside a 50% economic stake in SNVA Veranda Limited for vocational and global higher education.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Veranda Learning Solutions Ltd. delivers commerce professional-qualification coaching (CA, CS, CMA, CFA, CPA, ACCA), K-12 managed-school academic services, and government/competitive-exam test preparation (UPSC, banking, SSC, TNPSC, state PSCs) to school-age learners through working professionals across India. Programmes are delivered in offline, online, hybrid and blended formats through a pan-India network of Preferred Delivery Centres (PDCs) reaching Tier 2/3 cities, with a 50% economic interest retained in SNVA Veranda Limited (formerly SNVA EduTech) for vocational training and global higher-education pathways in the US and Europe.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Veranda Race Learning Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned; test-preparation content/brand; also a related party for brand-royalty cross-charge income
- Veranda XL Learning Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned; also a related party for sublease income and brand-royalty cross-charge income; proposed to be merged with the Company
- Veranda IAS Learning Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned
- Veranda Administrative Learning Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned
- Veranda Learning Solutions North America, Inc. — subsidiary: 100% owned; overseas subsidiary
- BAssure Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned
- Neyyar Academy Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned
- Neyyar Education Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned
- Veranda K-12 Learning Solutions Private Limited (formerly Educare Infrastructure Services Private Limited) — subsidiary: 100% owned; managed-school curriculum/K-12 operations
- J.K.Shah Commerce Education Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned; destination entity for the proposed demerger of the Commerce vertical
- Phire Learning Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 99.98% owned
- Navkar Digital Institute Private Limited — subsidiary: 65% owned
- Tapasya Educational Institutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 51% owned
- BB Publication Private Limited — subsidiary: 51% owned
- BB Virtuals Private Limited — subsidiary: 51% owned; also a related party for brand-royalty cross-charge income
- SNVA Veranda Limited (formerly SNVA Edutech Limited) — associate: 42.09% held; partnership for vocational and global higher-education business (Careerera, Euro American Education brands)
- Ms. Purnima Jitendra Shah — related party: Relative of Mr. Jitendra Kantilal Shah (former director); counterparty for rent paid by the Company

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Commerce: Strong performance, core driver of profitability; Non-Commerce (Govt Prep + Academic): Outperformed expectations, Govt Prep saw INR 5cr impairment but otherwise positive EBITDA; Vocational: Partial divestment to SNVA Veranda, retaining one North American entity temporarily.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Commerce Test Preparation:** J.K. Shah Classes, BB Virtuals, Navkar Digital Institute, Tapasya College of Commerce and Management, Logic School of Management
- **Academics / K-12:** Veranda K-12
- **Government Test Preparation:** Veranda RACE, Talent Academy, Veranda IAS
- **Vocational & Global Higher Education (SNVA associate):** Careerera, Euro American Education

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (pan-India, extending into Tier 2/3 cities via the PDC network)
- Tamil Nadu and Karnataka (managed CBSE and Cambridge International schools)
- United States and Europe (via SNVA Veranda associate brands Careerera and Euro American Education)
- International commerce credentials pathway (ACCA/CFA/CPA) for Indian students

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Enrollments reached 2.5 lakh students (+21% YoY); Collections at INR 449cr (+40% YoY); Managed college student base expected to grow from 17k to 19k+ in FY27.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: FY27 Revenue: ~INR 670cr (+40% YoY); FY27 PAT: >INR 144cr; Margin: Slight dip in Commerce EBITDA % due to new college OpEx/capex, recovering in FY28; Order Inflow: Targeting 19k+ students in managed colleges (+15%); Capex/Commissioning: 15 new managed commerce colleges in FY27; Karnataka expansion for Govt Prep.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Demerger of J.K. Shah Commerce (targeting INR 1,000cr revenue by FY30); Expansion of managed colleges into Tier 2/3 districts (15 new centers); Geographic expansion of Govt Prep into Karnataka, Andhra, Telangana; SNVA Veranda global university network expansion (US, Europe, Singapore).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained demand for government employment examinations across central/state government, PSUs and banking institutions, with increasing participation in competitive exams, is expected to support growth in Government Test Preparation
- India's higher education sector continues to expand, supported by rising enrolment levels, National Education Policy (NEP) reforms and growing emphasis on employability, creating opportunities in higher-education services and university partnerships
- The Indian education sector remains fragmented across segments, creating opportunities for consolidation and selective inorganic expansion
- Education remains a priority household expenditure, but prolonged macroeconomic uncertainty (slowdown, inflation, lower disposable income or employment prospects) could impact demand in certain discretionary learning segments and delay enrolment decisions
- Increasing availability of free educational content, self-learning platforms, AI-enabled learning tools and low-cost digital courses is shaping learner preferences and pricing dynamics across the sector, requiring continued investment in content quality and technology
- A significant share of the test-preparation business is linked to government recruitment and professional-qualification examination cycles, so delays in exam schedules or recruitment notifications can affect enrolment cycles and revenue visibility

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 EBITDA margin ~42%; FY27 Commerce margin expected to dip slightly due to upfront OpEx (rent, faculty, marketing) and soft capex for 15 new colleges; breakeven in Year 1, significant profitability from Year 2.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt repayment (deleveraging); Funding organic expansion (new colleges, geographies); Demerger to allow separate capital raising for Commerce vertical; Potential future M&A for global university assets via SNVA.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Veranda's FY27 expansion plans center on four priorities: geographic expansion, portfolio diversification, deepening presence across the education value chain, and strengthening existing verticals. The Government Test Preparation business plans to expand into Karnataka (using localised content, faculty capabilities and offline coaching infrastructure for KPSC and other state-level exams) and to build a stronger offline presence across North and West India, particularly Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Gujarat, to reduce regional concentration risk. In Commerce Education, around 15 new offline college locations are planned to accelerate growth and improve brand visibility and enrolments. The Company also plans to enter the Pre-KG managed-school segment and further expand its managed K-12 school portfolio as part of a long-term strategy to deepen engagement across the education lifecycle. Separately, the vocational/global higher-education business was restructured into a 50%-owned partnership (SNVA Veranda Limited, formerly SNVA EduTech Limited), which is projected to impact more than 200,000 learners annually, with a potential public listing envisaged at an appropriate stage. During the year the Group also completed a Qualified Institutional Placement and undertook debt optimisation (premature redemption of NCDs) to strengthen its balance sheet ahead of this expansion.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, focused on 'unlocking value' via demerger and structural profitability; Emphasizes disciplined execution and long-term vision (FY30 goals); Transparent about near-term margin trade-offs for growth.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- J.K. Shah Classes has over four decades of producing All India Rankers across CA, CS and CMA, giving the Commerce vertical institutional brand depth few commerce platforms can match
- ACCA exemptions of up to nine papers for qualified CAs give Indian finance professionals a differentiated, direct route into a globally recognised qualification
- Integrated B.Com-plus-professional-certification pathway lets students pursue a formal degree while simultaneously preparing for CA/CS/CMA, described as a genuine market differentiator
- Pan-India Preferred Delivery Centre network with vernacular-language coaching extends reach into Tier 2/3 cities underserved by English-only competitors
- Partnership with Cambridge University Press & Assessment gives Veranda K-12 schools access to globally recognised curricula and credentialing

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Lower CA pass percentages impacting demand; Regulatory delays in demerger (NCLT/SEBI); Execution risk in scaling 15 new colleges simultaneously; Faculty attraction/retention in Tier 2/3 towns; Impairment risks in non-core assets.

Shah entity and 35% to remaining Veranda; Warrants issued for prior acquisitions will be proportionately split between the two entities; Management views the 'Junior IAS' and integrated K-12-to-Professional pipeline as a unique moat against pure-play test prep competitors.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] Composite scheme of demerger of the Commerce vertical: Board approval Sep 2025, filed with NSE/BSE Sep 2025, exchange NOC Jan 2026, filed with NCLT Jan 2026, NCLT-directed CCM Mar 2026, CCM held and approved Apr 2026 (meeting held April 24, 2026), second motion filed Apr 2026, NCLT hearing "Orders Reserved on July 20, 2026", with "Listing in September 2026" of JK Shah Commerce Education Limited.
- [Demerger outlook] "Targeting 3-4x revenue growth via product and geographical expansion over 3-4 years; INR 1,000+ Cr revenue expected by FY30"; Commerce FY30 aspirations are "₹1,000+ Cr Revenue, 8 lakh+ Enrolments, 50%+ EBITDA Margin".
- [Divestment / JV] SNVA Veranda Ltd brings together "Veranda's domestic strength" and "SNVA's international network": "60+ Countries" presence, "1.5 million+ Trained Learners", combined presence across India, USA, UK, France, Italy, Malta, Switzerland and Singapore; FY27 targets of "₹250+ Cr Revenue", "₹50+ crore EBITDA", "2 lakh+ / year Learner Base" and "60+ countries", with FY26-FY30 outlook of 25% revenue CAGR, 35% EBITDA CAGR and "3x over 4 years" learner base.
- [Partnerships] "Feb 2025: Signed MoU with IIT Madras", "Jun 2025: Launches CIAP with IAB", "Jul 2023: Partnership with Logic School of mgmt."
- [Leadership] Chairman & Executive Director Mr. Kalpathi S Suresh — B.Tech. from IIT Madras, M.S. from Clemson University, selected for the 'Outstanding Entrepreneur of the Year' in 1999 by Ernst & Young, India.
